dominant_variable: Whether normalized retail-pharmacy cash earnings and return on invested capital could stabilize before debt, restructuring, healthcare expansion losses and dividend obligations consumed the apparent valuation discount.
business_thesis: Historical analogue: low multiples and a long dividend history can conceal a deteriorating earnings base. WBA is useful as a value/dividend-trap precedent because the core cash engine weakened while capital allocation and healthcare expansion failed to restore per-share economics.
counter_thesis: If pharmacy economics had stabilized, healthcare assets achieved acceptable returns and cash conversion supported the dividend, the depressed valuation could have offered mean-reversion upside.
market_expectation_assessment: Retrospective reconstruction. The key error is treating low P/E, high yield and prior dividend history as sufficient evidence of value without underwriting normalized FCF and balance-sheet resilience.
valuation_framework: Use normalized FCF after restructuring, lease/debt obligations and required reinvestment; treat dividend yield as an output of sustainable cash economics, not a valuation anchor by itself.
kill_criteria: Normalized FCF fails to cover reinvestment and distributions.
Dividend is cut because underlying cash economics deteriorate.
Healthcare expansion fails to earn adequate returns.
Balance-sheet or lease obligations force strategic retrenchment at unfavorable prices.
unresolved_evidence_gaps: No contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation is asserted.

provenance.note: historical analogue created in 2026; not evidence of contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation
